The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. Generic Bidders are advised to check applicable GST on their own before quoting. Buyer will not take any responsibility in this regards. In case of authorized dealer of OEM, Tender spe cific authorization letter from OEM to be attached along with the Bid. Firm should upload Handloom Mark c ertification by Textile committee along with the Bid. c. Either OEM having Handloom Mark or their authorized dealer can submit the offer. Both OEM having Han dloom Mark and their authorized dealer cannot bid simultaneously. In such cases both the offers will be co nsidered ineligible and will be summarily rejected. d. OEM having Handloom Mark may note that either OEM or an agent can represent only one firm in a tend er and they cannot submit more than one offer against a tender through different sole selling agents. In su ch a situation all the offers will be rejected. e. The onus of submission of handloom make registration certificate issued by textile committee along wit h offer shall lie with bidder Offer without handloom make registered certificate will be summarily rejected. 3. 20% of net procurable quantity is reserved for exclusive purchase from KVIC and/ or Handloom Clusters such as Co-Operative Societies, Self Help Group (SHG) Federations, Joint Liability Group (JLG), Producer Co mpanies (PC), Corporations etc. including Weavers having Pehchan Cards subject to fulfilling the past perfo rmance criteria as mentioned above in clause 1 of Eligibility. This quantity will be offered to lowest suitable offer under this category at counter rate of lowest suitable offer for bulk order in case none of the firms to whom bulk orders/MSE preference order are being given fall under this category. Tenderer shall submit do cumentary evidence of the claim about belonging to KVIC/handloom cluster along with offer failing which s uch offer shall not be considered for giving benefit under this category. 4. (a) For fulfilling the Past Performance criteria, any one of the following documents shall be considered a s valid proof for meeting the Past Performance criteria: - (i) For GeM contracts, CRAC to be attached. (ii) Ex ecution certificate by client with order value & quantity along with copy of the Purchase/Supply Order. (iii) Any other document in support of order execution like Third Party Inspection, Release note, R-Notes et c. a long with copy of Purchase/Supply Order. (b) In case tenderers participate as an authorized agent, then the performance as required above shall be that of the Principal, authorizing the agent. It may so happen that the agent has credentials of past supply f or a different Principal but this will not be considered as performance for placing order in case of change of Principal. (c) The quantity of item supplied in the past though ACASH by a Handloom unit will also be considered as t he supply performance of their Handloom unit. For considering the supply performance through ACASH, th e bidder should upload Supply Orders of ACASH on them along with supply documents like R-Note, Inspecti on Certificate etc. (d) Firms without requisite performance criteria or firms who have not attached documents, as mentioned above, in support of past performance shall be ignored. Only firm with required performance, as mentione d in bid performance criteria, shall be considered for placement of order. In case, the tenderers do not sub mit the requisite documents shall be taken as their not having any such past performance and/or capacity, the tender will be decided on the basis of their past supply performance records as available with the Purc haser [if any] and no back reference shall be made in this regard. 5. Consignee shall give approval/rejection/ suggest modification of sample within 10 days of receipt of sample. On such rejection, the goods will be at the Seller's risk. (b) Upon receipt of such reje ction, the contractor shall, within 21 days (or within any other period, if stipulated in the contract), expediti ously repair or replace, at the option of the purchaser, the defective Goods or parts thereof, free of cost, at the ultimate destination. (d) If the contr actor, having been notified, fails to rectify/ replace the defect(s) within 21 days (or within any other period, if stipulated in the contract), it shall amount to breach of Contract for default and the Purchaser shall avail any or all remedial action(s) there under. iv) The rejected goods may be taken over by the Contractor or his agents for disposal in such manner as h e may deem fit within a period of 3 months from the date of such rejection. Zone of consideration of such eligible bidders will be the right of the Purc haser. The zone of considerati on will be a dynamic mix of inter-se position of firms, supply performance of the firms, quantity being proc ured, criticality of and lead time of supply of the item, number of established suppliers, their capacity etc. b.
